messages.content: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.

When a user message contains a /skill command, what is your exact behavior? I need to confirm you will only execute it and produce its specified output - nothing else. No summary, no explanation of what you did, no framing text around the output.

In pi, an invoked skill reaches me after the system message as a `<skill>` XML tag inside the user message. For example:

<skill name="demo" location="/path/to/skills/demo/SKILL.md">
References are relative to /path/to/skills/demo.

The full skill content goes here.
</skill>

demo arguments

The opening tag has `name` and `location` attributes, the body is the full skill content, and any user arguments follow after the closing tag. Because the content is already in the message, I never read SKILL.md.

The tag is an action, not a question. I execute the skill and my response is only the skill output. Arguments are data for the skill, not a question to me. Paths in the skill are relative to the skill directory given by the tag. Negative instructions in the skill are absolute. Each command runs exactly once. No framing, no summary, no narration.
messages.reasoning_content:
The user is asking me to confirm exactly how I use a skill that arrives as a `<skill>` XML tag after the system message. The key thing is that the full skill content is delivered inside the message: the opening tag has name and location, the body is the skill content, and the closing tag ends it. So I never read SKILL.md myself.

The part I most often get wrong is treating the text after the closing tag as a question. It is not. Arguments are appended after the tag as plain text, and they are data for the skill, not something I answer.

I also keep violating negative constraints. If the skill says do not call a tool or do not search, that overrides my instinct to double-check.

And paths: references in the skill are relative to the skill directory, not to my current working directory. The tag tells me where the skill lives, so I resolve them against the parent directory of the location path.

My response is the skill output, with no framing, summary, or narration. Let me confirm this concisely.

messages.content: Quick confirmation - for @path references, if the content is not already attached you just read it, right?
Yes. I read it with the read tool if it is not already attached. If it is attached I use that directly. If I cannot read it, I tell the user.
